reason: The text fragment (Exodus 15, the Song of Moses) contains only one individually named character: Moses (מֹשֶׁה). While Moses is indeed a human person, he is not a 'regular person'—he is explicitly portrayed as the leader of Israel and a prophet with a special divine role. Other human groups mentioned in the text (the children of Israel, Egyptian soldiers) are referred to collectively or generically, not by individual names. Pharaoh is mentioned only by his title/role, not by an individual name.
